newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia agrees to supply India with LNG.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia agrees to supply India with LNG.

text.p: Indian Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister T.R. Baalu said on Wednesday that Indonesia had agreed to supply New Delhi with liquefied natural gas (LNG).

"We held discussions on LNG cooperation, and Indonesia has agreed to participate to supply LNG to India," Baalu told reporters after meeting officials from the mines and energy ministry and state oil company Pertamina.
Baalu, who is on a two-day visit to Indonesia, gave no further details.
Marzuan, an expert staff at the mines and energy ministry, said India had showed interest in buying LNG from Indonesia, but added that discussions were still at an early stage.
"There is intention from India to buy LNG from Indonesia. But India has many alternatives...to buy LNG from countries such as Oman," Marzuan told Reuters.
He said Baalu and his delegation were given a presentation on Indonesia's LNG supply system, including transportation.
"We also informed the Indian officials about the production sharing contract system in Indonesia," he said.

Indonesia is the world's largest exporter of LNG, with committed sales of more than 20 million tonnes annually. It was currently looking for buyers for its Natuna gas project, which has commercial reserves of 46 trillion cubic feet.
The project is expected to hit first production in 2003.
